Q: Powershell splitting string into chunks not working A:

Building on the helpful comments on the question:

Your immediate problem is that the (.NET) regex metacharacter . by default matches any character except a newline character (\n), so that splitting your multiline string into fixed chunks won't work as intended; to make . match \n too, you must activate the SingleLine .NET regex option, which you can do inline by prepending (?s) to your regex.

Thus, the immediate fix would be (sticking with the - potentially conceptually obscure[3] - use of PowerShell's -split operator):

# Using the inline form, (?s), of the SingleLine option 
$caption -split '(?s)(?<=\G.{1000})'

# VERBOSE EQUIVALENT:
# Pass the name of the option as the *3rd* RHS 
# operand to the -split operator, necessitating passing a *2nd one too*,
# purely *for syntactic reasons*, with 0 explicitly indicating
# the default behavior of not limiting the number of output strings.
$caption -split '(?<=\G.{1000})', 0, 'SingleLine'

However, there are (up to) two remaining problem(s) with this approach (apart from its conceptual obscurity):

  • If your input string's length is an exact multiple of 1000, -split's output array will contain an extra, trailing empty-string element.
    That said, you could filter out such an element, if present, as follows:

     $caption -split '(?s)(?<=\G.{1000})' -ne ''

    • Also note that the following alternative is likely to be faster with all but tiny chunk lengths (because lookbehind assertions ((?<=...)) are inherently inefficient), though with respect to memory efficiency it performs worse:[1]

      $caption -split '(?s)(.{1,1000})' -ne ''

  • A potential additional problem - on Windows only - is that if your input text happens to have Windows-format CRLF newline sequences rather than Unix-format LF-only ones, your substrings may end up with isolated CR and LF characters, if a splitting boundary happens to fall between them.

A more efficient[2] and conceptually clearer[3] alternative that avoids these problems (except for the Windows-only CRLF one) is to use the [regex]::Matches() .NET API instead, combined with PowerShell's member-access enumeration:

[regex]::Matches($caption, '(?s).{1,1000}').Value

[1] The reason is that use of a capture group ((...)) causes whatever such a group captures to be output too, along with the actual tokens between what the regex - meant to be a separator - matches; thus, each capture-group match in the output is surrounded by empty-string elements, thereby virtually doubling the number of output array elements.

[2] The efficiency, in terms of speed, comes from avoiding the need for costly lookbehind assertions. In terms of memory, with respect to the capture-group solution, it comes from avoiding the temporary inflation of the output array to virtually twice the final result size.

[3] The purpose of the -split operator is to specify a regex that describes separators between the desired output elements, whereas the task at hand is to describe the elements themselves, which only the [regex]::Matches() approach in this answer directly does.

Q: Using ffmpeg to get video info - why do I need to specify an output file? A:

An alternative to the answer using ffprobe from @blahdiblah, you can use null with ffmpeg:

ffmpeg -i C:\Test\3FA8D0E6-BD61-D160-98BB41304D63FAE3.mp4 -f null -

Q: Calculate age in day, month and year from birth date and a specific day using python A:

I think this is somewhat similar to what you're looking for:

from datetime import date

def age_calculator(birth):
    today = date.today()
    days = (today - birth).days
    months = 0
    years = 0
    while days >= 365.25:
        days -= 365.25
        years += 1
    while days >= 30.55:
        days -= 30.55
        months += 1
    return f'You are {years} years, {months} months and {int(days)} days old.'

user_year = int(input('Enter your birth year: '))
user_month = int(input('Enter the number of your birth month: '))
user_day = int(input('Enter your birth day: '))

print(age_calculator(date(user_year, user_month, user_day)))

I was checking if it's accurate and in some dates there is one day of inaccuracy... but I can't bother with figuring it out lol.

Q: Minecraft fabric with IntelliJ, failed to verify authentication A:

You can't delete this error from showing up. If you want to join a server on your minecraft account, use Auth me for fabric (https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/auth-me). Drop it in your /mods folder in IntelliJ project.

Q: 2's complement to signed binary converter using logic gates? A:

Previous answer is partially incorrect. It is correct to use not gates to get 1's complement, but to get the 2's complement you need sum and carry. The sum is performed by XOR gates and the carry is performed by AND gates. Each bit will need an NOT, an XOR and a AND gate. Connect each data line to an NOT gate (performing 1's complement) Connect one input of each XOR to one input of each AND. From now on I will refer this as input1. Connect the other input of each XOR to the other input of each AND. From now on I will refer this as input2. Connect each NOT output to its correspondent input1. Connect the input2 of less significant bit to VCC (logic level 1). Connect the output of less significant AND gate to the input2 of second less significant. (performing carry) Repeat last step for all gates. (cascating the carries) Leave the last AND output unconnected (in fact you do not need that last AND) The 2's complement of your data can be extracted from the output of the XOR gates.

Q: How do I use Chrome devtools MCP with multiple agents simultaneously? A:

It seems multiple instances of Chrome can not share the same user data directory, and devtools mcp only uses one data directory by default. But it's configurable.

Use isolated mode to give each instance a temporary profile.

npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --isolated

Or, for persistent storage, give each agent it's own data directory.

npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest --userDataDir "$HOME/my-devtools-profile"

I also add the --experimentalPageIdRouting flag for subagent coordination.
